A data frame is R's table type — a set of equal-length columns, each possibly a different type. This is what most real statistics and data analysis in R is built on.

```{=html}
<div class="sm-discuss">
  <p class="sm-discuss-label"><i class="fa-solid fa-comments"></i>Discuss first</p>
  <p>Before you run the code below: <code>students$score</code> is <code>c(92, 88, 95)</code>. Which rows do you expect <code>students[students$score &gt; 90, ]</code> to keep — how many, and whose?</p>
</div>
```

Edit the code below if you like, then press **Run Code** to check your answer.

```{webr-r}
students <- data.frame(
  name  = c("Ada", "Grace", "Rosalind"),
  score = c(92, 88, 95),
  pass  = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
)

students
summary(students$score)
students[students$score > 90, ]
```
